Class Toolkit

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.Toolkit
public final class Toolkit extends Object
Static factory methods for building UI elements with the DSL. Import statically to use: 
import static toolkit.dev.tamboui.Toolkit.*;

panel("Title",
    text("Hello").bold().cyan(),
    row(
        text("Left"),
        spacer(),
        text("Right")
    )
).rounded()

    • waveText

      public static WaveTextElement waveText(String text)
      Creates a wave text element with the given text.

      By default, a dark "shadow" moves through otherwise bright text. 

      waveText("Loading...").color(Color.CYAN)
waveText("Thinking...").inverted()  // Bright peak on dim text
      Parameters:
      text - the text to display
      Returns:
      a new wave text element

    • markupText

      public static MarkupTextElement markupText(String markup)
      Creates a simple inline markup text element that parses BBCode-style markup.

      For scrollable markup text with borders, use markupTextArea(String).

      Supported markup:

      • Modifiers: [bold], [italic], [underlined], [dim]
      • Colors: [red], [green], [blue], [yellow], etc.
      • Hyperlinks: [link=URL]text[/link]
      • Nested tags: [red][bold]text[/bold][/red]
      • Escaped brackets: [[ and ]]
      markupText("This is [red]red[/red] and [bold]bold[/bold].")
      Parameters:
      markup - the markup text to parse and display
      Returns:
      a new markup text element

      public static MarkupTextAreaElement markupTextArea(String markup)

    .scrollbar(ScrollBarPolicy.AS_NEEDED)
    .rounded()
    .focusable()
      Parameters:

      Returns:

    • lazy

      public static Element lazy(Supplier<? extends Element> supplier)
      Creates a lazy element that evaluates the supplier on each render.

      This allows state to be captured in the closure: 

      int count = 0;
lazy(() -> text("Count: " + count))
      Parameters:
      supplier - the supplier that provides the element
      Returns:
      a new lazy element

    • widget

      public static <T extends Widget> GenericWidgetElement<T> widget(T widget)
      Wraps any low-level Widget as a GenericWidgetElement.

      This is useful when you need to use a widget that doesn't have a dedicated element wrapper, allowing it to participate in the toolkit's styling and layout system. 

      widget(someWidget)
    .fg(Color.RED)
    .addClass("custom-class")
    .fill()

      Note: The styling applied to this element affects the element itself but may not propagate to the wrapped widget's internal rendering, as the widget renders directly to the buffer.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the widget
      Parameters:
      widget - the widget to wrap
      Returns:
      a new generic widget element
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if widget is null
